design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to galantamine PRC, galantamine, or placebo using an interactive voice response system.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was centralized via an interactive voice response system, ensuring allocation sequence generation and concealment, and baseline characteristics were balanced across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization to treatment was determined by calling an interactive voice response system immediately before medication was administered at visit 3. The subject number and treatment code (which corresponded to a specific medication kit) was randomly generated after the caller at the site provided the requested subject details.

domain_judgments.rationale: The double-blind design with matched placebos successfully masked participants and study personnel, protocol deviations were minimal, and an appropriate intent-to-treat framework was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: all treatments were supplied in opaque, size-0 gelatin capsules that were identical in appearance, taste and smell. Subjects received 1 capsule twice daily... All study personnel and participants were blinded to treatment assignment for the duration of the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Discontinuation rates were similar across groups (around 20-22%), and sensitivity analyses comparing observed cases and LOCF imputation showed consistent results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 768 (79%) randomized and treated patients completed the study... Results based on LOCF imputations for missing data on each of these primary efficacy variables were similar to the findings based on the OC data, and both are presented below.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome raters were trained, outcomes were measured consistently across groups, and both raters and participants remained blinded to treatment assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All raters were trained on outcome measures. The primary efficacy outcomes were the change from baseline to week 26 in ADAS-cog/11 score and the Clinician’s Interview-Based Impression of Change-plus caregiver input (CIBIC-plus) score... All study personnel and participants were blinded to treatment assignment for the duration of the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study adhered to a clear, pre-specified statistical analysis plan with explicitly defined primary and secondary endpoints reported transparently.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary efficacy analyses were the comparisons of galantamine PRC versus placebo in the change from baseline to week 26 for ADAS-cog/11 scores and distribution of CIBIC-plus scores.

overall_summary: This study was a well-conducted, double-blind, randomized controlled trial using centralized interactive voice response allocation, matched placebos, trained blinded raters, and consistent pre-specified analyses, resulting in low risk of bias across all domains.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomised, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled trial where patients were randomly assigned using a computer-generated schedule and sealed, opaque, numbered envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, allocation concealment was maintained using sealed opaque numbered envelopes, and baseline characteristics were balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The randomisation schedule was computer generated at the Janssen Research Foundation. The assignments were kept in sealed, opaque, numbered envelopes, each containing the allocation for the next patient.

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blinding was effectively maintained with identical placebos, and both intention-to-treat and observed-case analyses were conducted with consistent findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To help maintain blinding, all individual doses of galantamine and placebo were taken twice daily and were identical in appearance, taste, and smell.

domain_judgments.rationale: Between 13% and 25% of patients dropped out differentially across treatment arms due to adverse events, and missing data in the ITT analysis were handled using last observation carried forward (LOCF), which can introduce bias in progressive degenerative diseases.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 87% (186/215) of those in the placebo group compared with 80% (176/220) and 75% (163/218) in the lower and higher galantamine dose groups, respectively, completed the study... In this analysis, the last available assessment was carried forward into all subsequent assessment times for which actual data were not available.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome measures were standard validated instruments assessed identically across groups by assessors who were blinded to treatment allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The clinician’s interview was scored relative to baseline by a clinician blinded to other assessments and was based on separate interviews with the patient and the caregiver... To help maintain blinding, all individual doses of galantamine and placebo were taken twice daily and were identical in appearance, taste, and smell.

domain_judgments.rationale: All pre-specified primary and secondary efficacy outcomes were comprehensively reported according to the pre-defined statistical analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary efficacy variables used in the trial were the standard 11 item cognitive subscale of the Alzheimer’s disease assessment scale... and the clinician’s interview based impression of change plus caregiver input... Secondary efficacy variables were the expanded (13 item) version... and the disability assessment for dementia scale

overall_summary: The study was well-conducted and double-blinded with adequate randomization and allocation concealment. However, there are some concerns regarding missing outcome data due to differential dropout rates across treatment groups and the reliance on last observation carried forward imputation for a progressive condition.

design_rationale: Eligible patients were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to galantamine or placebo according to a central randomisation code generated by the sponsor.

domain_judgments.rationale: A central randomisation code was generated by the sponsor, and baseline characteristics between the two groups were well balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After a 4-week, single-blind, placebo run-in period, patients were randomly assigned placebo or galantamine 24 mg/day for 6 months according to a randomisation code generated by the Janssen Research Foundation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind using identical tablets, protocol deviations were low, and analyses followed intention-to-treat principles.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Galantamine and placebo were administered as identical single tablets taken orally twice daily.

domain_judgments.rationale: There was substantial and differential attrition between groups (25.8% galantamine vs 16.8% placebo), largely due to adverse events, and analyses relied on observed cases and LOCF imputation, which may not adequately handle informative missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The proportions of patients continuing in the trial were 84·6% (n=335) in the galantamine group and 92·9% (n=182) in the placebo group at 6 weeks, 79·0% (n=313) versus (89·3% (n=175) at month 3, and 74·2% (n=294) versus 83·2% (n=163) at month 6. Thus, more galantamine patients than placebo patients discontinued the trial, mostly as a result of adverse events (19·7% vs 8·2%).

domain_judgments.rationale: Standard validated dementia scales were used, and assessors were blinded, with an independent masked clinician assessing the global rating scale.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To avoid any potential unmasking of treatment allocation, an independent (masked to other components of the study), experienced, trained clinician undertook the CIBIC-plus assessments to provide an overall impression over the course of the trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Analyses followed a prespecified statistical plan with predefined primary endpoints, covariates, and analysis models, and results were consistently reported across specified outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Scores on ADAS-cog/11, ADAS-cog/13, neuropsychiatric inventory, and disability assessment in dementia were compared by an a-priori-defined ANOVA model, with treatment and country as factors... To test for potential bias due to effects of assessment time and repeated measurements from the same patient on the primary efficacy outcome, a prespecified longitudinal analysis of ADAS-cog/11 was also done with a mixedeffects model

overall_summary: The overall judgment is some concerns due to differential participant dropout (25.8% in the galantamine group vs 16.8% in the placebo group) primarily driven by adverse events, analyzed using observed-case and last observation carried forward methods. All other domains had low risk of bias.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to galantamine (24 or 32 mg/d) or placebo using a computer-generated code.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence generation was computer-generated, but the method of allocation concealment is not explicitly described, leading to some concerns.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Following a 4-week, single-blind placebo run-in period, patients were randomly assigned (using a computer-generated code) to one of two oral galantamine treatment groups or placebo.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind using identical tablets, protocol deviations were low (10%) and balanced across groups, and intention-to-treat analyses were conducted alongside observed cases.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Galantamine and placebo were administered as identical single tablets taken twice daily... Throughout the 12 months, investigators remained blinded to the treatment to which patients had been randomly assigned at the start of the doubleblind phase.

domain_judgments.rationale: There was substantial overall attrition (31% missing primary endpoint at 6 months) with marked differential dropout driven by adverse events in the galantamine arms (23% and 32% vs 8% in placebo), and handling missing data primarily by observed cases or single imputation (LOCF) may not adequately prevent bias in a progressive disease like Alzheimer's.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 764 patients screened for the initial phase, 636 were randomly assigned to trial medication, of whom 438 (69%) completed the double-blind phase... Discontinuations due to adverse events during the double-blind phase were more common in galantamine-treated patients than in those receiving placebo (23% in the 24 mg/d group and 32% in the 32 mg/d group versus 8% with placebo)

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors, patients, and caregivers were blinded using identical placebo tablets, and validated, standardized cognitive and clinical rating scales (ADAS-cog, CIBIC-plus) were used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Galantamine and placebo were administered as identical single tablets taken twice daily... Throughout the 12 months, investigators remained blinded to the treatment to which patients had been randomly assigned at the start of the doubleblind phase.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary and secondary outcomes were predefined and consistently analyzed according to prespecified statistical plans with both OC and ITT (LOCF) analyses reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary analysis of 6-month efficacy data were based on patients who also provided postbaseline data for any of the ADAS-cog/ 11, CIBIC-plus, or DAD variables at designated assessment times—a traditional “observed cases” (OC) analysis. Furthermore, to confirm the robustness of the efficacy results, a more conservative 6-month intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis was performed using the last-observation-carriedforward (LOCF) method

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high due to substantial overall and differential missing outcome data (approximately 31% overall attrition, with 23% and 32% discontinuation due to adverse events in active arms vs 8% in placebo), analyzed primarily using complete cases and LOCF imputation. Other domains exhibited low risk or some concerns.

design_rationale: The study is described as a multicenter, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, double-blind randomized clinical trial where patients were randomized using a computer-generated code.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence generation was random (computer-generated code), tablets were identical ensuring concealment, and baseline characteristics were balanced across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Following a 4-week single-blind, placebo run-in period, patients were randomized to one of four treatment arms for 5 months, using a computer-generated code (weeks 1 to 21)... Baseline characteristics of the different treatment groups were comparable (table 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind with identical matching placebos, deviations were low and balanced across groups, and both observed-cases and intention-to-treat analyses were conducted with consistent results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Galantamine and placebo were administered as identical single tablets taken orally twice daily... Furthermore, to confirm the robustness of the efficacy results, more conservative intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses were performed using the last observation carried forward method (the last postbaseline observation available for each patient who received treatment).

domain_judgments.rationale: Completion rates were approximately 80% across all groups with similar proportions and reasons for discontinuation, and ITT (LOCF) analyses confirmed the primary findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 1178 patients screened, 978 were randomized to trial medication, of whom 80% completed the study... Treatment discontinuations due to adverse events were low in all galantamine groups (6 to 10%) and comparable with the discontinuation rate in the placebo group (7%).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome measures were standardized validated clinical scales in Alzheimer's disease (ADAS-cog, CIBIC-plus, ADCS/ADL, NPI) and assessed under double-blind conditions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The CIBIC-plus was scored by a trained clinician, based on separate interviews with the patient and the caregiver... Galantamine and placebo were administered as identical single tablets taken orally twice daily.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary and secondary outcomes were analyzed according to a prespecified sequential step-down closed testing procedure, and all defined outcomes were fully reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For the primary efficacy measures, an a priori sequential, step-down, closed testing procedure was used to allow multiple statistical comparisons between each galantamine group (starting with the 24-mg/day group) and the placebo group, while maintaining the Type I error rate (a) at 0.05.

overall_summary: The study is a well-designed, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial with low risk of bias across all five RoB 2 domains.
